architecturalAssertions.assertion: Built1769–1771 as a large brick institutional block around two courtyards; projecting bays and corner strips define the facade.
Central projecting bay carries a triangular pediment with a clock.
architecturalAssertions.confidence: high for assembly; current clock partly tree-occluded;1880reference shows pediment

architecturalAssertions.assertion: Broad stone-framed doors and lanterns occupy the end bays; they historically separated elderly residents and orphans.
architecturalAssertions.confidence: high; current leaf-off2024view confirms museum west door, steps and lanterns

architecturalAssertions.assertion: Current risalits/recesses yield3+3+5+3+3bays. Low basement openings, tall lower windows, medium middle tier and shorter upper tier have pale multi-pane frames.

architecturalAssertions.assertion: Hip roofs enclose both courts; centre front/rear pediment roof slopes show green metal. Narrow brick chimney masses rise above the principal ridges; at least two pale canal-side dormers remain visible.
architecturalAssertions.confidence: high for roof layout; medium for dormer count and green metal assignment; cap ornament simplified

architecturalAssertions.assertion: The lower later wing has three principal tiers, a complicated shorter roof, and a rounded corner with a pale glazed cupola. It belongs to the same current BAG parent.
architecturalAssertions.confidence: high for scope/silhouette; cupola face positions and peak height approximate
